messages:
jess (Product): Heads up — flight to Madrid got changed last week. Airline issued a voucher for €120 that they applied to my agency account, then charged me a €45 change fee to my company card for the new itinerary. I submitted an expense but it got flagged because the voucher isn't on my statement. How should I document this?
maria (Finance): That happens sometimes with agency bookings. Voucher is a non-cash airline credit; we need proof of the voucher value and evidence that the company actually incurred the €45 fee. Attach: airline voucher email (code + amount), booking confirmation showing original fare and new fare, and your company card charge for €45.
tom (Travel Ops): If the voucher was issued to the travel agency instead of you, request a short confirmation from the agency (email) stating voucher code, amount, and that they applied it to your booking. That counts as supporting docs.
expenses-bot: Reminder: upload PDFs/PNGs under 5MB. If the voucher is on the agency portal only, a screenshot with URL + timestamp is accepted.
jess (Product): I can get the agency confirmation but it might take 24h. Meanwhile, can I still expect the expense to reimburse the change fee?
maria (Finance): Yes — the €45 change fee is reimbursable as a travel expense. We'll hold the voucher credit as an offset: when we process the expense, we'll net the voucher against the total cost if the company bears the fare. If the agency applied the voucher and reduced the billed amount to the company card, we need that card statement line.
linda (Manager): Approving now pending docs — I confirm this was a company trip and the change was work-required.
jess (Product): One more wrinkle: voucher shows a service fee withheld on the airline email (voucher: €120, usable value €115). Do we net the €115 or €120?
maria (Finance): Use the usable value (what the voucher actually covers) — attach the voucher terms/email that show the usable amount. We'll treat any service/processing fees as non-recoverable unless refunded separately.
jess (Product): Cool. Also need to confirm currency conversion rules — airline emailed in EUR, company billing is USD.
maria (Finance): Convert voucher value and fee to USD using the airline voucher issuance date FX rate. Paste the conversion used into the "Expense notes" field or a screenshot from our converter: https://expenses.redwood.com/fx-convert. We'll verify.
jess (Product): Uploading agency email + airline voucher screenshot now. Marking expense EXP-21055 in notes.
expenses-bot: Files received. Expense ID: EXP-21055. Missing: agency confirmation if voucher not on your statement.
tom (Travel Ops): If the agency can't provide a confirmation, we can accept a written attestation from the agent plus your manager's approval.
maria (Finance): Final note on VAT: if the airline shows VAT on invoice and you're claiming it, include the VAT line. Otherwise we treat fares as non-recoverable VAT unless we have a proper invoice.
jess (Product): Thanks all — I'll chase agency and upload attestation if needed. Appreciate the quick answers :pray:
maria (Finance): No problem. Once docs are complete we'll process the €45 reimbursement and apply voucher offset if applicable. Expect ~3 business days after docs are final.
